name: Qualify inbound leads from HubSpot forms with Clay and Claude and book meetings

parameters.content:
## Qualify inbound leads from HubSpot forms with Clay and Claude and book meetings

Sales teams that reply to demo requests hours later and qualify by hand.

### How it works
Trigger: Any form submission or demo request posts to the workflow; chat-widget conversations and inbound emails to sales@ use the same path.
1. Receive the submission
2. Enrich
3. Score against the ICP
4. Read the message
5. Route
6. Notify the rep with context
7. Update the CRM
8. Follow up on silence
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Clay / Apollo / Clearbit, HubSpot / Salesforce, Slack + Calendly.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Edit the qualification criteria and the routing rules in the Config node; swap Clay for Apollo or Clearbit.
Guardrail to keep: The first reply commits to nothing: no pricing, no availability, no promises — it acknowledges and asks.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/inbound-lead-qualification/

## 1. Receive the submission
Name, email, company, message, source page and UTM parameters

## 2. Enrich
Company size, industry, tech stack, funding and the contact's role from Clearbit, Apollo or Clay

## 3. Score against the ICP
Deterministic ICP score from firmographics and role, plus intent points for the source page, message content and repeat visits

## 4. Read the message
Extracts the use case, urgency and any objections from the free-text message and drafts the first reply: acknowledges what they asked, asks the one qualifying question you always ask, offers a booking link for hot leads

## 5. Route
Hot: rep notified in Slack and the reply goes out immediately

## 6. Notify the rep with context
Company snapshot, role, score and why, the message, the draft reply and a suggested opener for the call

nodes.name: Section: 6. Notify the rep with context

parameters.content:
## 7. Update the CRM
Contact and company created or updated with enrichment, score, source and the qualification answer when it arrives; the lead is stamped with response time

## 8. Follow up on silence
If a hot lead has not replied or booked in 24 hours, a second short message goes out; after 72 hours the rep is prompted to call

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Web forms, chat widget, sales inbox
- Enrichment (Clearbit, Apollo, Clay)
- CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive)
- ICP definition and scoring thresholds (sheet)
- Calendar / booking links

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Read the message" step of the Inbound Lead Qualification Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Extracts the use case, urgency and any objections from the free-text message and drafts the first reply: acknowledges what they asked, asks the one qualifying question you always ask, offers a booking link for hot leads.

Rules:
- The first reply commits to nothing: no pricing, no availability, no promises — it acknowledges and asks.
- Free-mail and suspicious submissions are never enriched with paid credits.
- Reps can override routing; overrides are logged and feed the threshold review.
- Response-time and meeting-rate by score band are reported monthly to check the ICP model.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Read the message
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

Route

Hot: rep notified in Slack and the reply goes out immediately. Warm: reply goes out, added to a nurture sequence, weekly digest to sales. Cold or spam: polite reply or none, CRM updated.
